papers.title: Fabrication and Characterization of AISI 420 Stainless Steel Using Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) offers great possibilities to fabricate metal tools with a complex geometry, but there are limitations regarding some materials. This work focuses on the fabrication of AISI 420 stainless steel using SLM for the application of plastic injection mold. The melt characteristic of the powders was firstly concluded, and then the microstructure, phase composition, and hardness were characterized using scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and Rockwell hardness test, respectively. The results showed that cellular microstructure was observed along the direction of the maximum heat flow. The proportion of the phases varies with the change of SLM processing parameters, which directly affects on the hardness of the parts. The relative density over 99% was obtained and the highest hardness presents 50.7 HRC, which meets the requirement of plastic injection molding application.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究AISI 420模具钢的选区激光熔化，不涉及生物医学植入物或骨整合，与用户研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: It focuses on tool steel for injection molds, not biomedical implants; no porous structure, stress shielding, fatigue, or osseointegration reported.

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate AISI 420 stainless steel components by selective laser melting for plastic injection mold applications.
summary_en.method: Characterized melt pool features, microstructure evolution, phase composition, and Rockwell hardness.
summary_en.result: Attained over 99% relative density and a maximum hardness of 50.7 HRC, meeting mold requirements.
summary_en.validation: Validated via scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and hardness testing.
